svg.title: Proposal and award status path
svg.desc: Five stages. Internal approval can take several approval steps while In Review, such as department and OSP. It ends at Approved, which starts sponsor submission at Unsubmitted. Internal approval moves to Rejected when the proposal is stopped before sending, including from Unsubmitted when the deadline is missed. Sponsor submission ends at Accepted, which starts sponsor decision at Pending. Received and Validated are optional, since some sponsors do not report them. A Failed attempt is resent. An Invalid or Recalled attempt returns to Unsubmitted and is signed off again. A proposal sent back before consideration moves from Pending to Sent Back, then to Unsubmitted, and is signed off again. A sponsor can ask for changes before deciding, such as just-in-time information, which moves Pending to Changes Requested and then to Intent to Award, Awarded, or Declined, or back to Pending. Intent to Award can go back to Changes Requested. When the sponsor never decides, Pending or Changes Requested moves to No Decision; a late sponsor decision still moves it on. A sponsor can return a proposal as Not Reviewed. A Withdrawn proposal ends or is revised. Sponsor decision ends at Awarded, which starts acceptance at Terms Review. Terms are accepted as offered, or negotiated, with On Hold while bargaining is paused, ending at Accepted or Not Accepted; Not Accepted can return to Negotiating. Accepted starts the award at In Setup. An optional Preliminary Setup, an at-risk account, can open at Intent to Award or Awarded; the award still goes through acceptance and setup.
svg.text: Other records, such as modifications and subawards, have their own statuses.
Rejected can come from any point before sending,
by an approval step, the PI, or a missed deadline, including from Draft
fix the package, sign off again
Withdrawn can also come from Intent to Award
A late sponsor decision still moves it
to Intent to Award, Awarded, or Declined
Bargaining rounds are kept as Negotiation records.
